notes:
I couldn't write the Proverbs 27 notes. None of the sources loaded, so I have nothing verified to report.

I tried to open four pages at once: the Enduring Word chapter on Proverbs 27, the Precept Austin page for Proverbs 27, the Bible Hub page on 27:17, and Geneva Bible notes on StudyLight. A coding error in how I handled the results meant I never saw what came back. When I tried again, the tool told me I'd used all my calls for this turn. I didn't get a single page's content.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge, with a URL for every point. So I haven't written notes from memory with links I never read.

If you send another message, I can start over in smaller steps: read each page separately and check it loaded before going on. I'd go in this order:

1. **The usual reading of each verse:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and the Bible Hub and StudyLight pages for Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Matthew Henry and others.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon, Desiring God and Ligonier sermons on particular verses. Likely ones are v. 1 (boasting about tomorrow), v. 6 (a friend's wounds), v. 17 (iron sharpens iron) and v. 20 (Sheol and Abaddon). I'd only claim a real disagreement if the sources show one.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible translator notes (especially on vv. 9, 16, 19 and 21), Bible Odyssey, and Catholic and Orthodox sources (New Advent's Church Fathers, catholic.com, oca.org).

Because so many pages are involved, it might work better to ask for a few verses at a time, say vv. 1–9, then 10–18, then 19–27.
